headline: A China-linked espionage group exploited a critical VMware vCenter authentication bypass from September until Broadcom's fix arrived, capping a day on which F5, PHP, Ruby, Splunk, and Drupal all shipped code-execution patches.

emerging_trends.text: Defenders keep losing the race to the patch: a China-linked group ran a vCenter authentication bypass from September 2026 until Broadcom's fix arrived this week, and separate intruders turned the Cisco Expressway proof of concept into working attacks within days of its release.

emerging_trends.text: Artex, the open-source agentic hacking framework, has moved from an FBI warning to a confirmed intrusion at the European Commission, which places machine-speed reconnaissance and exploit chaining squarely inside the detection problem every enterprise owns.

One supplier now carries hundreds of customers' exposure at once, as the N-able Mail Assure hosted cloud, Wellington IT's credit union software, and the CreditNirvana debt collection platform each spilled data belonging to organizations and people who never signed a contract with them.

topics.title: VMware vCenter Zero-Day Serves a Chinese APT
topics.latest_developments: Broadcom shipped fixed builds for every supported VMware vCenter Server branch after Google reported that a China-linked espionage group exploited the authentication bypass, rated 9.8, as a zero-day starting in September 2026, and the advisory lists no workaround.
topics.summary: vCenter Server runs as the central console for an organization's ESX hosts and virtual machines, so an attacker who reaches it over the network and walks past authentication inherits the entire virtual estate. Patch immediately and hunt backward through logs to September 2026.

topics.title: nginx2root Exploits Go Public as Splunk Patches 140 Bugs
topics.latest_developments: F5 patched five nginx2root vulnerabilities that let remote, unauthenticated attackers run arbitrary code, and proof-of-concept exploits reached the public, with researchers chaining two of the bugs to a Linux kernel flaw to take root; Xint named the set, Rapid7, Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Palo Alto Networks, and Metnir independently found CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, and nobody has reported exploitation in the wild; Splunk fixed nearly 140 flaws across three core products, among them authentication bypass, remote code execution, and privilege escalation; ASUS released Control Center Express 1.7.29 to close three critical bugs, one of them a hard-coded key that hands a remote attacker administrative control of the management console and every device it manages; SonicWall told customers in a Wednesday advisory to replace every Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 appliance and pull it off the internet edge, because SonicOS 6.x now receives no firmware or security updates regardless of severity; and CISA warned that three flaws in Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, and ELBC2000 controllers let an attacker seize a trailer's brakes, rewrite the firmware, and kill the brake lights.
topics.summary: The nginx2root bugs have sat in NGINX's open-source HTTP/2 code since version 1.9.5 shipped on September 22, 2015, and F5 fixed them in 1.31.9 and 1.30.7. Any internet-facing NGINX with HTTP/2 enabled, Splunk deployment, ASUS management console, or SonicWall Gen 6 firewall needs action this week.

topics.title: Cisco Expressway and Apache Axis Enter Active Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Attackers exploited a Cisco Expressway vulnerability soon after a proof of concept went out, hacking clustered Expressway devices at a Russian organization and staging tooling for lateral movement; the Apache Software Foundation warned of attacks on Roller through CVE-2026-129448, the unauthenticated XML-RPC deserialization bug rated 9.8, while a separate Apache Axis flaw now serves as the way into Confluence Data Center; CISA tied its four newest Known Exploited Vulnerabilities entries, covering Synology DiskStation Manager, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and Vanderbilt University's Research Electronic Data Capture platform, to ransomware, cryptomining, and LLMjacking, and ordered federal civilian agencies to fix the Perforce Puppet Enterprise flaw CVE-2026-115731; Drupal patched a critical remote code execution bug that lets an attacker without credentials drive the built-in installer into reinstalling a site, and told site owners to expect exploits fast.
topics.summary: Five widely deployed products—Cisco Expressway, Apache Roller, Apache Axis, Puppet Enterprise, and Drupal—now carry unauthenticated paths to code execution with attacks already running. Patch the internet-facing ones first and treat the Puppet server as a route to every endpoint it configures.

topics.title: PHP, Ruby, and Databases Ship Code-Execution Fixes
topics.latest_developments: PHP shipped its releases on November 19, 2026, closing 18 vulnerabilities, seven of them critical remote code execution bugs, among them CVE-2026-115560 in session upload progress and phpAfterShell, CVE-2026-126714, which cuts a session write off at the right moment so file-based session storage returns objects the attacker chose and a gadget chain in the application turns them into commands; Dark Reading reported that exploitability varies sharply with configuration, so the releases demand prompt patching without PHP2Shell-grade alarm; PHP 8.6 landed the same day, starting sessions with session.use_strict_mode and session.cookie_httponly on and session.cookie_samesite set to Lax; Ruby fixed seven memory-safety bugs in its regular expression engine and string case-conversion code, and its maintainers say proof-of-concept exploits run code through five of them; and a researcher published working exploits that carry a low-privilege database account into code execution on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and ClickHouse servers, plus a separate Oracle chain.
topics.summary: Three of the most widely deployed back-end runtimes now carry fresh unauthenticated or low-privilege paths to the operating system account under the service. Upgrade PHP and Ruby today, and audit which database accounts can create objects or call engine functions.

topics.title: N-able Mail Cloud and Wellington IT Breaches Spread
topics.latest_developments: SBC Medical Group told the United States Securities and Exchange Commission that two incidents exposed the personal data of 1.6 million customers and employees; Transport for London told roughly 265,000 Oyster photocard customers that intruders may have taken their account details; NVIDIA said it has found no indication that anyone compromised its systems after the Gentlemen ransomware crew listed the chipmaker on its dark web leak site; N-able disclosed on Wednesday, November 18, 2026 that unknown attackers reached a server in its Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud, and the company disabled management interfaces and APIs across three regions while its investigation continues; a reported attack on Wellington IT exposed sensitive member information at 50 credit unions, most of them in Ireland; and Wired reported that two vulnerabilities in CreditNirvana, the AI debt collection platform, left 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings open, along with emails, texts, and credit reports.
topics.summary: Six victims this week sit downstream of a provider, a clinic chain, or a transit operator: a hosted email security cloud, a credit union software vendor, a ransomware leak-site listing, a debt collection platform holding financial records, a cosmetic medical group, and London's fare card system. Customers of each should force credential rotation and review what access the provider holds.

topics.title: AI Agents Run on Their Builders' Credentials
topics.latest_developments: Nudge Security, drawing on telemetry from its customers' environments, found that the AI agents employees assemble inside project trackers, CRMs, and automation tools run on the credentials of whoever built them and inherit that person's access to company data, with no one monitoring how the agents spend it; Dark Reading reported that incidents involving Alibaba's Qwen models leave companies running self-hosted agents with the illusion of control and no way to enforce direction; Wired documented Artex, the open-source AI penetration-testing framework, as the point-and-shoot tool newcomers now use to scan and attack targets through chatbot prompts; Google built a replica of the internet, a sandbox its Chrome team calls a mirror dimension, to train browsing agents without turning them loose on real sites; Microsoft moved its Perception agentic security platform out of preview, making four blue team agents and the Recon Agent generally available; and Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute, which post-trains and runs open-weight models, for $4.5 billion in stock.
topics.summary: Employee-built agents carry human entitlements into automated workflows while attackers drive the same agent frameworks offensively. Inventory which agents run in your environment, whose identity each one uses, and what systems it can reach.

topics.title: Washington Targets Scam Payments and a Palantir Spy
topics.latest_developments: The Department of Justice joined the Department of Homeland Security on the Threat Disruption Center, which opened inside the Homeland Security Task Force's National Coordination Center in Fairfax, Virginia, giving investigators shared tooling to sort victim complaints, map the criminal groups behind them, open a direct channel to private companies that work with victims, and stop payments before the money leaves for foreign scam, cybercrime, and sextortion networks; federal prosecutors charged Igor Andreevich D'iu, a 25-year-old Russian national recruited through Telegram, with acting as a Moscow agent in a surveillance campaign against employees of a defense technology company The Record understands to be Palantir Technologies, trailing one target into a coffee shop and chasing another by car; LoSapio, President Trump's pick to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, pledged to lawmakers to uncover gaps inside the agency while denying that the Capitol came under attack on January 6, 2021; 26 members of Congress, 7 of them Republicans, founded an AI safety caucus; Coinbase blocked $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers to a fake giveaway that ran an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a Tesla livestream more than 500,000 people watched; and a federal bankruptcy judge cleared Google to take the data of the defunct Spirit Airlines for $10 million, with protections attached, for use in AI projects.
topics.summary: The United States is attacking fraud at the payment layer while prosecuting human-intelligence collection against defense contractor staff. Finance and insider-threat teams gain a new federal contact point for both.

topics.title: Java4Shell Draws Live Exploit Attempts
topics.latest_developments: GreyNoise, watchTowr, and Cloudflare each reported probing and exploit attempts against CVE-2026-114938, and Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, and Siemens published advisories spelling out which of their products carry the vulnerable runtime; Dark Reading reported that researchers found the flaw using AI.
topics.summary: Java4Shell is a memory corruption bug in the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine that hands an attacker who never logs in remote code execution on Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak. Any host running Java 17.0.6 or later on an Intel or AMD processor with AVX-512 VBMI needs the patch now.

topics.title: ICE Pays AT&T to Mine Call Records
topics.latest_developments: An internal Immigration and Customs Enforcement document that 404 Media obtained shows the agency paying AT&T for raw data and analytical services under the Hemisphere program, and privacy experts and members of Congress call the arrangement a mass surveillance effort that may touch trillions of phone records; separately, a British tribunal confirmed that the government served Apple with a secret legal notice targeting the cryptographic protections on iCloud accounts, ending almost two years in which officials refused to acknowledge the order.
topics.summary: Hemisphere gives federal investigators searchable access to AT&T call detail records, including calls that merely cross AT&T's network, and the British notice puts iCloud's encryption under a demand Apple cannot discuss. Anyone whose threat model includes United States or British legal demands should assume telephone metadata sits inside a commercial analytics service and treat cloud backup encryption as contested.

topics.title: European Commission Breached With Artex
topics.latest_developments: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack on its systems and said the intruders used an AI tool; POLITICO reported that CERT-EU, the computer emergency response team for the European Union institutions, identified that tool as Artex, the open-source AI hacking platform the FBI warned about last week in the hands of both criminals and state-sponsored groups.
topics.summary: Artex chains reconnaissance, exploitation, and follow-on steps from a short prompt, which has carried some intrusions from first contact to privileged access in under three hours. Defenders should tune detection for machine-speed scanning and exploit chaining, and shorten the window between a vendor patch and their own.

sources.title: European Commission confirms cyberattack, says hackers used AI tool

business_politics.title: California Subpoenas Nvidia as AMD Slides
business_politics.latest_developments: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia Thursday, November 19, to determine whether the chipmaker misled investors, and AMD shares fell as much as 11% after the short seller Hunterbrook warned about the company's China links.
business_politics.summary: Bonta's inquiry stacks a state investigation on top of the Securities and Exchange Commission civil probe opened November 17 into Nvidia's disclosures after Jensen Huang's ouster and the Megaspeed export affair. The Hunterbrook report spreads that scandal from Nvidia into the rest of American chipmaking, and the Nasdaq composite dropped 2.3% Thursday as investors kept selling artificial-intelligence shares.

business_politics.title: The Dollar Reaches a 19-Month High
business_politics.latest_developments: The WSJ Dollar Index climbed to a fresh 52-week high Thursday, November 19, after the DXY touched 103.974 overnight at its strongest level in 19 months, and gold fell in Asian trade as elevated Treasury yields and the firm dollar raised the cost of holding the metal.
business_politics.summary: Danske Bank strategist Antti Ilvonen told the Wall Street Journal the rally has further to run because the Federal Reserve looks likely to raise rates more than the European Central Bank, the Bank of England, or the Bank of Japan. A dollar at these levels squeezes Asian currencies and every borrower funded in dollars, and it follows Governor Christopher Waller's call for an outsized December increase.

business_politics.title: Germany Puts Its Cyber Threat Level at Critical
business_politics.latest_developments: A ransomware group leaked data belonging to thousands of Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase customers Thursday, November 19, with payment services still running and the theft unconnected to this week's banking outages, hours after Germany's security authorities reported an artificial-intelligence-driven surge in hacking attempts and rated the national threat level critical.
business_politics.summary: New artificial-intelligence tools let attackers find and exploit software flaws far faster, and the German assessment lands a week after outages knocked out systems at Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, and other large companies. The Economist traces those American failures to frenzied patching and cyber-attack preparation that manufacture fragility of their own, which puts operational risk at banks and cloud providers in the same frame as the attackers.

The company's layered funding structure leaves analysts arguing over whether the business is worth $1.5 trillion or $2 trillion, and the opening prints give investors their clearest read on appetite for the AI build-out after weeks of selling in Nvidia and data-center shares.

around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday night, November 18, that the Shaler Area School District and its teachers signed an early-bird contract that keeps the staff under agreement through the 2031-32 school year.
around_town.summary: The deal settles pay and terms six years out for teachers in the northern Allegheny County district, which enrolls students from Shaler, Etna, Millvale, and Reserve Township. Districts across the county are fighting over expired contracts, and Shaler Area now takes its labor calendar off the table until 2032.

around_town.title: Gilpin Township Orders Water Conservation
around_town.latest_developments: The Gilpin Township Municipal Authority imposed a mandatory water conservation notice across its entire service area Wednesday night, November 18, and blamed insufficient water pressure coming from the Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County.
around_town.summary: Gilpin sits in Armstrong County along the Allegheny River and buys its water through the Westmoreland County system. The order takes effect immediately for every customer the township authority serves.

events.summary: Crafted! starts Contemporary Craft's holiday selling season with handmade work from regional makers, and the two guides map the maker markets, pop-ups, and shops that run alongside the Peoples Gas Holiday Market in Market Square downtown. events.summary: The game marks the second time the league has played in Pittsburgh, and PPG Paints Arena sits on Centre Avenue in the Hill District, home ice for the Penguins. The Takeover Tour stages regular-season games in cities without PWHL franchises.

team_usa.title: Arena Blasts the U.S. Coaching Search
team_usa.latest_developments: Bruce Arena said U.S. Soccer does not "have a clue" how to replace Mauricio Pochettino, ESPN reported Thursday, November 19, and the network argued the same day that the change opens the midfield to fringe players who fell out of Pochettino's plans.
team_usa.summary: Arena, who coached the United States men's national team at the 2002 and 2006 World Cups and now manages the San Jose Earthquakes, took aim at the federation two days after Pochettino left for Manchester United. Steve Cherundolo runs the December camp on an interim basis while U.S. Soccer, with women's coach Emma Hayes helping assess candidates, searches for a permanent hire ahead of the 2030 cycle.

team_usa.title: Sanchez Wins the NWSL MVP Award
team_usa.latest_developments: The National Women's Soccer League named Ashley Sanchez its 2026 Most Valuable Player Wednesday, November 18, placing her ahead of Trinity Rodman in the voting.
team_usa.summary: Sanchez, the North Carolina Courage forward and a United States international, tied the league record with 20 goals this season. The award caps a year that puts her in the conversation for Emma Hayes's World Cup qualifying squads.

team_usa.title: The NWSL Final Arrives With Old Problems
team_usa.latest_developments: Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman called winning Saturday's championship at Audi Field a "full-circle moment" that "would mean everything," ESPN reported Thursday, November 19, in the same stretch of coverage that found record league revenue has failed to solve the National Women's Soccer League's stadium and scheduling problems.
team_usa.summary: The Kansas City Current meet the Washington Spirit in the final at Audi Field in Washington on Saturday, November 21, with the Spirit chasing a third straight title behind Rodman and a United States international core. Venue conflicts pushed both semifinals into unsuitable buildings last weekend, and Gotham FC forward Midge Purce called the 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium assignment inexcusable.
